# Base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Prevents interactive prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies for LAMMPS
# build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make
# cmake: Build system generator for LAMMPS
# git: To clone the LAMMPS source code
# wget: General utility, sometimes needed for fetching dependencies
# libfftw3-dev: Required for Fast Fourier Transform support in LAMMPS (e.g., for KSPACE package)
# ca-certificates: For secure network connections (e.g., git clone)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    libfftw3-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest development branch of the LAMMPS source code
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b develop https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps

# Configure and build LAMMPS using CMake
# - We create a build directory as is standard practice with CMake
# - CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER are set to the MPI wrappers provided by the base image to ensure MPI support.
# - PKG_REAXFF=ON: Enables the ReaxFF package as requested.
# - PKG_KSPACE=ON: Enables long-range electrostatics (e.g., PPPM), a common requirement.
# - PKG_MOLECULE=ON: Enables molecular dynamics simulations.
# - PKG_RIGID=ON: Enables simulations with rigid bodies.
# - FFT=FFTW3: Links against the FFTW3 library we installed.
# - The build is parallelized using make -j$(nproc) for speed.
RUN cd /opt/lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
      -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=ON \
      -D PKG_KSPACE=ON \
      -D PKG_MOLECULE=ON \
      -D PKG_RIGID=ON \
      -D FFT=FFTW3 \
      ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled LAMMPS executable to a system-wide location on the PATH
RUN cp /opt/lammps/build/lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Verify that the lmp executable is in the PATH
RUN which lmp

# Set a default working directory for running simulations
WORKDIR /workspace

# Copy the HNS ReaxFF example files into the working directory to be readily available for test runs
RUN cp -r /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Set the default command to run a shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# MiniCluster manifest for running a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment
# Environment: AWS ARM-based CPU instances in Kubernetes, spanning up to 4 nodes.
# Application: LAMMPS from ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-hns-test
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to start with for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the test on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The maximum number of pods the MiniCluster can scale to.
  # This is set to 4 to allow running across multiple nodes as required.
  maxSize: 4

  # The number of tasks for the job. If not set, Flux will default to one task per pod.
  # For this test, we let Flux use all available slots on the single node.
  tasks: 1

  # Flux Operator specific settings
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for ARM instances
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # This is required for ARM instances. Note that since 'disable' is true,
      # this image will not actually be used, but the setting is included for completeness.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

      # Crucially, we disable the flux sidecar container.
      # This assumes that the main application container has the 'flux' executable on its PATH.
      disable: true

  # Set strict logging for better debugging and error reporting.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Ensure the job and pods are not deleted after completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the application container to be run by the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend 'flux run -n <tasks> ...' to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # The main container is not a launcher, it's the application workload.
      # This MUST be false as per instructions.
      launcher: false

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS EFA network devices.
      # This is necessary for high-performance interconnect on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-hns-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 7 -v y 7 -v z 7 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
    optionFlags: -o cpu-affinity=per-task
  logging:
    strict: true
  maxSize: 4
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST parse a result to include the units for katom or Matom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
You MUST set flux.optionFlags to "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
